opps.title: Flexible configuration scoping
opps.desc: Account structure forces manual overhead for franchises, regional groups and multi-brand setups. Decisions made at setup get locked in and cause downstream pain.
opps.evidence: High — 5 evidence points, 22% workaround stat, 4 named merchants
opps.business: High — blocks 1→5M scaling; structurally caps growth for franchise / multi-brand
opps.urgency: High — competitive risk (36% mention better PSPs); merchants create dummy stores today
opps.dependency: Yes — every other opp operates within the account-structure model
opps.why: Scores high on all four signals. Under-invested due to org complexity, not strategic unimportance.

opps.title: Scalable deployment of settings & assets
opps.desc: No bulk apply across merchant accounts or stores; deploying configs and assets is manual at fleet scale.
opps.evidence: High — Adidas Olympics miss, 36% competitive comparison, top survey request
opps.business: High — directly enables campaign revenue moments
opps.urgency: High — already costing real money (Olympics missed)
opps.dependency: Partial — depends on O1 to be fully effective
opps.why: Quantified business loss plus competitive pressure. The Adidas anecdote alone justifies P0.

opps.title: Settings transparency & override management
opps.desc: 73% override at device level; inheritance logic is opaque; no overview of what is set where.
opps.evidence: Highest — 7 evidence points, “only 27% never overridden”, usability-test failures
opps.business: High — directly serves the 15% support-reduction target (inheritance drives tickets)
opps.urgency: High — confusion compounds with fleet size; worsens as Adyen scales
opps.dependency: Yes — every self-service feature depends on transparency
opps.why: Most evidence of any opportunity plus a direct line to the 2026 OKR. Strongest case in the tree.

opps.title: Submerchant activation kit
opps.desc: Activation is the #1 pain for AfP platforms; manual workarounds at scale. First boot, passcode and Wi-Fi are major friction.
opps.evidence: Highest in B-journey — Tide 200/mo, Fresha 4h/day, Palisis 30%, Munu 5%
opps.business: High — caps AfP segment growth (Adyen's fastest-growing area)
opps.urgency: High — losing platforms to competitive PSPs implicitly
opps.dependency: No — but cross-squad fragmentation makes it harder, not less important
opps.why: Highest quantified evidence in either journey plus strategic AfP importance. Coverage fragments across squads.

opps.title: Device customization at scale
opps.desc: MVP exists for SFO1 only; not extensible across fleet or models; merchants want segment-based content.
opps.evidence: Medium — 5 evidence points from Branding research only
opps.business: Medium — supports merchant brand investment, no direct 2026 OKR hit
opps.urgency: Medium — desirable but not blocking; MVP exists for SFO1
opps.why: Real demand but the business case is “merchant satisfaction” rather than a quantified Adyen-side outcome.

opps.title: Merchant self-service & role-based access
opps.desc: Many settings require Adyen support intervention; access controls within the merchant org are missing.
opps.evidence: Medium-High — 5 evidence points including the AllSaints escalation
opps.business: High — directly serves the 15% support reduction
opps.urgency: Medium — manageable today, but every new merchant adds friction
opps.dependency: No — depends on O3 to be safe
opps.why: Strong evidence plus outcome link. Delivered through O3 work. Could be P0 if weighted on support target alone.

opps.title: Setting taxonomy & shared language
opps.desc: No shared definitions; misleading names; unclear merchant-facing vs internal classification.
opps.evidence: High — 6 evidence points with concrete examples (contactless floor limit, télécollecte, EventUrl)
opps.urgency: Medium — slow burn; worsens with scale and new markets
opps.dependency: Yes — every self-service capability degrades without it
opps.why: Strong evidence, but cost is spread across many small tickets with no single Olympics-style anecdote. Could be P0.

opps.title: Branded packaging & preboarding
opps.desc: Platforms carry shipping, branding and preboarding overhead outside their core business.
opps.evidence: High within IPP — 4 quantified evidence points
opps.business: Medium — platform stickiness, not a direct Adyen revenue line
opps.why: Real opportunity, but not Devices-owned. P2 reflects tracking for completeness, not active ownership.

opps.title: Dynamic / personalized terminal content
opps.desc: Signals for transaction- or loyalty-driven content; no current way to deliver.
opps.business: Unclear — no quantified business case yet
opps.why: Demand is real but the use case is unproven. Mantel's 68-category content is interesting, not a roadmap commitment.

opps.title: Configuration lifecycle controls
opps.desc: No scheduling, no TEST↔LIVE parity, no rollback for setting changes.
opps.evidence: Medium — 5 evidence points in a “what we lack” framing
opps.urgency: Medium — infra investment substantial, user-facing missing
opps.dependency: Yes — TEST↔LIVE, scheduling, rollback are platform capabilities
opps.why: Infra work is happening. Risk: infra ships without user-facing scope. Would be P0 if infra stalled.
